content: On Saturday, November 13, 2010, the following interviews and discussions are scheduled: At 1:15 PM, Dr. Adrian F. Hernandez, Dr. Christopher M. O'Connor, and Dr. Randy Starling will discuss the ASCEND-HF trial, which evaluates the clinical effectiveness of Nesiritide in patients with decompensated heart failure. The embargo on this information will lift at 5:23 PM on Sunday, November 14, 2010. At 1:45 PM, Dr. Clyde Yancy will provide a historical perspective on the ASCEND trial and its implications for patient care. At 3:15 PM, Dr. Manesh Patel, Dr. Ken Mahaffey, and Dr. Keith Fox will present findings from the ROCKET AF trial, which compares the efficacy of Rivaroxaban to Warfarin for stroke prevention in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. The embargo will lift at 10:55 AM on Monday, November 15, 2010. At 3:45 PM, Dr. Zubin Eapen will share insights from the perspective of a cardiology fellow attending the AHA 2010 conference. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Christopher M. O'Connor and Dr. Robert Harrington will discuss Duke University's presence at the AHA conference, including ongoing activities and expectations. The 5:00 PM and 5:30 PM time slots are open. On Sunday, November 14, 2010, the following sessions are planned: At 1:00 PM, Dr. Deepak Voora will discuss a study that uses a whole blood RNA signature to classify platelet function on aspirin in healthy volunteers, highlighting a common underlying pathway. The embargo will lift at 3:15 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Kenneth Ellenbogen will present the primary results of the ADVANCE Bridge to Transplant trial, which compares different programming strategies for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). The embargo will lift at 4:39 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. At 2:00 PM, Dr. David Cohen will discuss the PARTNER trial (Cohort B), which evaluates health-related quality of life outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation versus non-surgical therapy in inoperable patients with severe aortic stenosis. The embargo will lift at 4:55 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Jonathan Piccini will present findings on the association between sustained ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation and increased mortality following non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndromes. The embargo will lift at 12:00 PM on Wednesday, November 17, 2010. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Thomas Povsic will discuss a pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic substudy of RB006, a direct Factor IX inhibitor, in patients with acute coronary syndromes. The embargo will lift at 11:00 AM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. The 3:30 PM time slot is open. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Karen Alexander will address two topics: the growing burden of cardiovascular disease in the elderly and the risk of loss of independence in frail older adults following myocardial infarction. The embargoes for these topics will lift at 5:45 PM and 11:00 AM on Monday, November 15, 2010, respectively. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Renato Lopes will discuss the process of building a small data coordinating center. At 5:00 PM, Dr. Tracy Wang will present findings on the under-utilization of emergency medical services among patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction, based on data from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry. The embargo will lift at 4:08 PM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. On Monday, November 15, 2010, the schedule includes: At 9:00 AM, Dr. Christoph Kaiser will discuss the BASKET PROVE trial, which examines late cardiac death and myocardial infarction associated with late stent thrombosis in large vessel stenting. The embargo will lift at 11:39 AM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. At 9:30 AM, Karen S. Pieper will present insights from the PLATO trial, suggesting that proton pump inhibitor use is more likely a marker of higher cardiovascular risk rather than a direct cause. The embargo will lift at 9:15 AM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Kristin Newby will provide updates on the MURDOCK study and discuss challenges and opportunities in biomarker research. At 10:30 AM, Prof. Murray Esler will present findings from the Symplicity HTN-2 trial, which evaluates renal sympathetic denervation for hypertension treatment. The embargo will lift at 12:01 PM on Wednesday, November 17, 2010. At 11:00 AM, Dr. Otavio Berwanger will discuss the ACT trial, which evaluates the efficacy of acetylcysteine in preventing contrast-induced nephropathy. The embargo will lift at 12:01 PM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. At 3:00 PM, Dr. The embargo will lift at 12:01 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Keith Aaronson will discuss the ADVANCE Bridge to Transplant trial, which evaluates the HeartWare® HVAD system for advanced heart failure. The embargo will lift at 4:17 PM on Sunday, November 14, 2010. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Matthew Price will present the GRAVITAS trial, which compares standard versus high-dose clopidogrel based on platelet function testing after PCI. The embargo will lift at 10:55 AM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. At 4:30 PM, Dr. James Daubert will discuss QTc prolongation during therapeutic hypothermia and its clinical significance. The embargo will lift at 6:45 PM on Saturday, November 13, 2010. At 5:00 PM, Dr. Renato Lopes will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference in Portuguese. The schedule for Tuesday, November 16, 2010, and Wednesday, November 17, 2010, continues with similar detailed discussions and embargoed trial results.
